Let \(N=\binom n2\). For each unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\), define
\[
x_{ij}(\sigma)=
\begin{cases}
1,& i\text{ appears before }j\text{ in }\sigma,\\
0,& j\text{ appears before }i\text{ in }\sigma.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent-swap distance is Kendall tau distance:
\[
d(\sigma,\tau)=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}|x_{ij}(\sigma)-x_{ij}(\tau)|.
\]
Indeed, each adjacent swap changes the relative order of exactly one pair, and sorting \(\sigma\) into \(\tau\) requires exactly the number of pairwise relative-order disagreements.

For \(p=1\), if \(\sum_\sigma c_\sigma=0\), then for one cut coordinate \(x_{ij}\),
\[
\sum_{\sigma,\tau}c_\sigma c_\tau |x_{ij}(\sigma)-x_{ij}(\tau)|
=-2\left(\sum_{\sigma:x_{ij}(\sigma)=1}c_\sigma\right)^2\le 0.
\]
Summing over all \(\binom n2\) pairs gives \(1\)-negative type.

For any \(p>1\), since \(n\ge4\), the four permutations
\[
1234\cdots,\quad 2134\cdots,\quad 1243\cdots,\quad 2143\cdots
\]
form an isometric square with side lengths \(1\) and diagonals \(2\). Taking coefficients \(+1,-1,-1,+1\) around the square gives
\[
2(2^p+2^p)-2(1^p+1^p+1^p+1^p)
=4(2^p-2)>0,
\]
so \(p\)-negative type fails. Hence
\[
\wp=1.
\]

At \(p=1\), equality holds exactly when every cut contribution vanishes:
\[
\sum_{\sigma:x_{ij}(\sigma)=1}c_\sigma=0
\quad\text{for every }1\le i<j\le n,
\]
together with \(\sum_\sigma c_\sigma=0\). Thus \(E\) is the orthogonal complement of the span of
\[
1,\ x_{ij}\quad (1\le i<j\le n).
\]
These \(1+\binom n2\) functions are linearly independent: if
\[
a_0+\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}x_{ij}(\sigma)=0
\]
for every \(\sigma\), swap adjacent entries \(i,j\) in a permutation where they are adjacent. Only \(x_{ij}\) changes, so \(a_{ij}=0\). Then \(a_0=0\).

Therefore
\[
\dim E=n!-1-\binom n2.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(1,\ n!-1-\binom n2\right)}
\]
